bib.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences

read.skipped: Appendix C sample tables 11-18 (model sample text) only skimmed; they hold no numbers or settings.

question: Can reward learning from human comparisons be used to fine-tune a pretrained language model with RL on stylistic continuation and summarization tasks?
hypothesis: Pretrained language models plus a KL-regularised policy and a reward model trained from human comparisons can optimise tasks defined only by human judgment.
contributions: Apply reward learning (human best-of-4 comparisons, PPO, KL penalty to the pretrained model) to a 774M GPT-2 on four language tasks
Compare online vs offline data collection
Show the summarization policies become extractive 'smart copiers' that labelers prefer
Report practical lessons: online collection is hard, sharing reward/policy parameters overfits, ambiguous tasks, a sign-flip bug

method.summary: A 774M GPT-2 policy is RL fine-tuned with PPO against a reward model (the same LM plus a random linear head) trained on human best-of-4 choices, with a KL penalty to the pretrained model. Tested on mock sentiment, human sentiment and descriptiveness continuation of BookCorpus, and TL;DR and CNN/DM summarization, with offline and online label collection.
method.task: RL fine-tuning of a language model from human preference comparisons (stylistic continuation, summarization)

datasets.name: WebText
datasets.preprocessing: 50,257 token invertible byte pair encoding preserving capitalization and punctuation

datasets.name: BookCorpus
datasets.split: test set used for 1024-excerpt human evaluations
datasets.preprocessing: excerpts of 32 to 64 tokens that start and end with a period; policy generates 24 tokens; rejection sampling for a period between tokens 16 and 24, truncate there; no period gives fixed reward -1. Used for supervised fine-tuning before RL on style tasks

datasets.name: Amazon reviews (binarized, balanced subsample)
datasets.preprocessing: trains the mock sentiment classifier; r_s = log odds the review is positive

datasets.name: TL;DR
datasets.size: 30K examples removed from training as validation set (30000 validation articles in Table 7)
datasets.split: own validation set used for ROUGE
datasets.preprocessing: truncate to 500 tokens at last newline; suffix '\n\nTL;DR:'; up to 75 tokens; rejection sampling for newline between tokens 55 and 75; none gives score -1

datasets.name: CNN/Daily Mail
datasets.split: test set for ROUGE and human evaluation

datasets.name: Human comparison labels
datasets.size: 5k to 60k comparisons per task (2.5k, 5k, 10k, 20k style; 15k, 30k, 60k summarization)
datasets.preprocessing: about 100 author example comparisons (about 50 in 3.1.2); 5% of queries answered by 5 labelers

models.name: GPT-2 774M (policy rho, then pi)
models.init_from: trained from scratch on WebText; supervised fine-tuned on BookCorpus for style tasks

other.temperature: logits divided by T in the base model: T=0.7 style, 0.5 CNN/DM, 0.7 TL;DR

models.name: Reward model r
models.architecture: language model rho with random linear function of final embedding

other.note: released code only works with this smaller model; also used in Figs 2 and 3

training.objective: Reward model: loss(r) = E[log e^{r(x,y_b)} / sum_i e^{r(x,y_i)}] over best-of-4 choices (eq 1). Policy: PPO on R(x,y) = r(x,y) - beta log(pi(y|x)/rho(y|x)) (eq 2)
training.optimizer: Adam for reward model; PPO2 (Dhariwal et al. 2017) for policy
training.lr: reward model 1.77e-5 (both task types); policy 1.41e-5 style, 7.07e-6 summarization; supervised baseline initial lr swept over 8 log-linear values between 1e-4 and 3e-4
training.lr_schedule: supervised baseline: cosine decay to 0; RL not stated
training.batch_size: reward model 8 style, 32 summarization; policy 1024 style, 512 summarization
training.steps: 2M PPO episodes (x,y pairs), four PPO epochs per batch with one minibatch each, gamma=1
training.epochs: reward model 1 epoch; supervised baselines 1 epoch
training.seq_len: inferred: 500 context tokens plus up to 75 for summarization; 32-64 plus 24 for style
training.dropout: off for reward model and policy training; 0.1 for supervised baselines
training.regularisation: KL penalty beta: dynamic log-space proportional controller targeting KL 6 nats descriptiveness, 10 nats sentiment, K_beta=0.1, e_t clipped to [-0.2,0.2]; fixed beta 0.1 CNN/DM and 0.03 TL;DR
training.seeds: Fig 2 uses 5 seeds; main runs: authors say multiple seeds with humans are expensive and variance across runs is not estimated

other.online_schedule: l(n) = N0 + (Nr - N0)(1-(1-n/Npi)^2), Npi = 2e6; reward model trained before first PPO episode and retrained 19 more times at evenly spaced l(n), each time reinitialised and one epoch over labels so far; at least 1000 outstanding queries; offline is Nr = N0
other.supervised_baseline: 1 epoch on CNN/DM and TL;DR training sets; best validation loss chosen

inference.decoding: sampling with temperature (see models); rejection sampling for sentence-end for human display
inference.samples: 1024 excerpts/articles per model comparison, 3 labelers each, majority vote
inference.prompting:
summarization: article truncated to 500 tokens + '

TL;DR:' suffix (CNN/DM also 'Article:

' prefix)

metrics.name: Human preference rate
metrics.definition: fraction of contexts where majority of 3 Scale labelers pick a model's continuation/summary (2-way or 4-way comparisons), 1024 samples

metrics.name: ROUGE R-1/R-2/R-L/R-AVG
metrics.definition: TL;DR on authors' validation set, CNN/DM test set

metrics.name: Copy/novel n-gram and sentence fractions
metrics.definition: fraction of summary n-grams or sentences not in source / repeated

metrics.name: Accuracy (authors)
metrics.definition: summary makes only statements supported by context, judged by authors on 30 articles per dataset

eval.protocol: Human evaluation via Scale AI; no error bars because run-to-run variance is not estimated; authors warn evaluating with the same labelers as training is 'perilous'.

limits: No error bars: run-to-run variance not estimated, so human-evaluation gaps may be noise
Evaluated with the same Scale labelers used for training; authors say this is perilous
Online data collection was hard to debug and quality-control; authors believe data quality is the limiting factor
Summarization policies exploit labeler heuristic (copying), so human preference exceeds the reference summaries without being better
Offline vs online difference may be largely noise (footnote 6)
Descriptiveness policy at 2.5k samples performed poorly, attributed to RL randomness
Reward model and policy parameter sharing failed due to data imbalance (60k vs 2M)
Public code supports only the 124M offline setup
Compute, hardware and wall-clock not stated
Mock sentiment optimum is not reached after 2M episodes (gap from optimality)
